title: Dawnstead - First True Dawn
_note: Richer-register curtain-call (the south's one allowed era step-up). era snes (8 voices, chords allowed, warm reverb) - still rendered on the chip engine for cohesion. 100 BPM, 4/4, C major, fully radiant. The emotional summit of the whole dusk->dawn arc. Lead (pulse25-warm) carries the Tinderwick lullaby; a soft warm COUNTER-LEAD weaves a counter-melody quoting the Dimglass route's BOUNCED Vesper contour (town & road themes embracing at the finish). Harp arpeggio (pluck) + a soft sustained PAD bed for genuine chords. Warm full bass with real low-end motion. Drums = fuller gentle groove, triumphant fill + crash at seam. Vesper FULL BLOOM across two voices at once. 24-bar loop ~58s (the brief names 32 bars/~51s; 24 bars balances the curtain-call grandeur with the stated duration and gives the two leads room to trade).

tracks.name: lead
tracks._note: The Tinderwick lullaby, radiant and confident. Vesper full bloom: G3->C4->D4 lift reaching up to C5, E4->D4->C4 settle. 24 bars: A (1-4) state, A (5-8), B-bloom (9-16) lifts highest, A (17-20) return, tag (21-24) bloom into the loop. Final bar leans on G (V) into bar 1.

tracks._note: Soft warm 2nd lead weaving the Dimglass route's BOUNCED Vesper contour (G->C->D bounced, springy) as a counter-melody answering the lullaby. Sits below/between the lead, mostly in its rests. Town & road embracing.
